grammar · A1

Instructions with the imperative

Learn how English uses the base verb for clear directions, instructions, warnings, invitations, and appropriately softened requests.

≈ 60 mingrammarspeakingfunctional language3 learning objectives
NoticeFollow useful instructions.
DiscoverSee why the listener is understood.
BuildSequence and soften instructions.
UseGuide another person clearly.

Notice before the rule

First-day instructions

Come in. Please take a seat. Write your name here. Don’t sign the second page. Ask me if you need help.

  • What form begins each instruction?
  • Is the subject you written?
  • How does the negative instruction begin?

Get to the root: the listener is understood

An imperative begins with the base verb because the subject you is normally understood from the situation. The speaker directs the words toward the listener: (You) open the file. English leaves you unspoken because it is already obvious.

The grammar is compact, but the social meaning depends on context. Turn left can be helpful directions. Take one tablet with food can be medical instructions. Don’t move can be an urgent warning.

Purpose Pattern Example
Positive instruction base verb Save the document.
Negative instruction don’t + base verb Don’t delete the original.
Polite direct request please + imperative Please send me the address.
Shared suggestion let’s + base verb Let’s check it together.

Tone changes the relationship

A bare imperative can be neutral, friendly, urgent, or rude. Instructions on a screen are neutral. The same form spoken to a coworker may need please or a request with Can you…?

Form Typical effect
Send me the address. clear and direct
Please send me the address. polite, but still direct
Can you send me the address? framed as a request
Let’s check the address. includes speaker and listener

Use it in real life

Give directions: Guide the teacher from your home to a useful place nearby.
Explain a process: Explain how to join a video call or make your favorite hot drink.
Friendly host: Welcome a visitor using five appropriate instructions, offers, or invitations.

Reflect

Explain why the subject is normally absent in an imperative. Then give one positive instruction, one negative warning, and one softened request.

Final check: form, meaning, and tone

1. ___ the document.

2. ___ here.

3. Which option includes both people?
